name: Griffin Bastion

civilization.name: The Talon Concordance
civilization.notes: Avian-mammalian hybrid species organized into aerie-cities atop mountain peaks. Sophisticated oral tradition and gliding-based transportation networks.

geological_features: Mountain ranges reaching 18km in altitude due to low tectonic plate density
Vast highland plateaus connected by natural stone bridges
Deep rift valleys with their own isolated microclimates
specific_features: Aerie-cities built into cliff faces with intricate wind-tunnel architecture
A network of signal fires visible from orbit during seasonal ceremonies
resources: Titanium-rich ore veins in the mountain cores
Rare crystalline formations prized for optical instruments
Geothermal energy from rift valley vents
description: Griffin Bastion is a world that reaches upward. Its mountain ranges are among the tallest recorded on any terrestrial planet, their peaks piercing the upper atmosphere where the air thins to near-vacuum. Between these vertical monuments stretch highland plateaus of windswept grassland, connected by natural stone arches that span kilometers and serve as highways for the planet's dominant species. The rift valleys far below are humid, forested, and almost entirely unexplored by the inhabitants above.

The wind is constant and purposeful here, shaped by the extreme topography into predictable currents that the Talon Concordance has mapped over millennia. Their cities are built to channel these winds, creating a constant low harmony that serves as both climate control and cultural expression. Standing at the edge of an aerie-city, one looks out over a vertical world where distance is measured not in kilometers but in altitude.

The Talon Concordance evolved from a gliding ancestor species, developing true powered flight through a combination of biological adaptation and ingenious wing-augmentation technology crafted from mountain crystals and cured hide. Their civilization is organized around the concept of elevation as status, with the highest aeries reserved for their philosopher-navigators. They have no written language but maintain an oral tradition of staggering complexity, their harmonic speech capable of encoding information in ways that resist translation.

First contact protocols are in effect, and Griffin Bastion is officially quarantined from general traffic. A single observation post in geosynchronous orbit monitors the Concordance's development, but the temptation to intervene grows as titanium prospectors push for access to the mountains. The Concordance is aware of the orbital presence, incorporating the steady light into their cosmology as a new kind of star. What they will do when they learn its true nature is a source of considerable anxiety among the contact team.
